titulo: How a $1,000 card balance grows without you buying anything 💳
descripcion: Credit card interest compounds: you pay interest on interest. A 2% monthly rate turns $1,000 into about $1,268 in a year. Educational content, not financial advice.

escenas.texto: You owe one thousand dollars on a credit card. You don't buy anything else. A year later, you owe almost thirteen hundred.
The trick is compound interest. Every month, interest is added to your balance. Then next month, you pay interest on that interest too.
With two percent a month, it doesn't add up to twenty four percent a year. It's closer to twenty seven.
And minimum payments are designed to mostly cover interest, so the debt barely shrinks.
The good news: compound interest works for you too, when you save instead of owe.
Pay the full balance when you can, and compounding stops working against you. Follow for more money explained.
